newsitem.title: USA: McDermott says profitable FY97 unlikely.
newsitem.headline: McDermott says profitable FY97 unlikely.

text.p: McDermott International Inc said Thursday that the losses it recorded in the first half of the 1997 fiscal year portend an unprofitable full fiscal year.
The energy services company said that it expects 1997 to follow the trend of posting a second half that is "significantly less profitable" than the first half.
However, interim Chairman and Chief Executive James Dutt said in a statement that "expected gains from the planned sale of surplus assets should partially offset lower second half results."

For the second quarter reported Thursday, the company posted a net loss of $12.43 million, or $0.27 per share, compared with a net profit of $9.1 million, or $0.13 per share, during the prior year's second quarter.

The company said it hopes to improve the profitability of its core businesses: the marine construction business of its J. Ray McDermott SA affiliate and the power generation and U.S. government business of its Babcock & Wilcox.
It also intends to cut costs and sell non-core assets.
